summary: Low-impact CLI guidance change. decrypt drop stops asking users to remove the forward manifest entry, encrypt status shortens its reversed flag, and the agent-facing skill now instructs users to retain the entry. The removed manifest lookup was used only to construct the cleanup instruction. Migration generation, recorded events, coverage checks, apply-time SQL, and dual-write guidance are unchanged. Targeted tests assert the new output but were not run. No material release-failure scenario was established; normal review is appropriate.

behaviour_changes.description: decrypt drop no longer performs the final manifest lookup or prints an instruction to delete the forward manifest entry after applying the migration. It still preserves that entry, records encrypted-dropped, and tells users to keep dual-writing until application.

encrypt status displays 'reversed' instead of 'reversed (remove from migrations.json)'. The existing condition still requires the encrypted column to be absent and its reverse state to be encrypted-dropped.
The stash-cli skill describes retaining the manifest entry as the final reversed state and explicitly prohibits manual editing, replacing its previous cleanup instruction.

evidence.claim: After writing the migration and recording its event, the base calls manifestPlaintextFor solely to conditionally print the manual manifest-removal instruction.
Head retains event recording and the migration application, dual-write, and schema-cleanup guidance, while omitting the final manifest lookup and manual manifest-removal instruction.
Base renders 'reversed (remove from migrations.json)' for the reversed missing-column case.
Head still derives reversed from the encrypted counterpart's encrypted-dropped state and checks physical absence before rendering the shortened 'reversed' flag.
Tests exist for ordinary missing-column drift and reversed output without a migrations.json instruction. Status: exists_not_run.
The changed test asserts that manifest removal is not called, completion guidance omits migrations.json, and the dual-write-until-applied instruction remains. Status: exists_not_run.
The reverse-drop guidance says the manifest entry remains, reversed is its final state, manual editing is prohibited, and dual-writing must continue until migration application.
The planner reads the manifest and forward state for each declared column, prints a comparison with targetPhase, and performs no migration or manifest mutation.

Pair resolution prefers explicit or active recorded plaintext targets, then uses manifestPlaintextFor as a fallback. The helper maps encryptedColumn or its naming convention to the manifest's plaintext column.
The exact base-to-head diff changes only the helper import, post-event manifest lookup, comments, and completion text in this file; drop guards and generated SQL are unchanged.
